_comment: Generic architecture contract for governed path placement.
This file owns the SCHEMA and the ROLE VOCABULARY only.
It deliberately contains NO absolute machine paths: the machine instance is
owned by hwz-ops (ops/workspace/environment.yaml#roots) and is supplied by
the caller. Servers, hosts and checkouts differ; roles do not.
See 11-topology-authority-ownership: serveros owns schema, hwz-ops owns instance.

roots_source.note: Machine instance. Never duplicated here. If this file grew absolute paths, the ownership split would be violated.

_run_pattern_note: DERIVED FROM THE MACHINE, not invented. Every Run directory under
ARTIFACTS_ROOT/skills/ was read: 24 of 25 are RUN-<yyyymmdd>-<slug>
The previous value was '^RUN-[0-9]{4,}$'. On this machine it matched
exactly one directory -- the legacy outlier sitting at the CANCELLED
skills/<skill>/<project>/<RUN> level -- and rejected all 24 real ones.
A declared pattern that describes the accident and not the practice is
worse than no pattern: a resolver following it would have refused every
Both shapes are accepted so that a read of an existing Run is never
denied. New Runs use the date-slug form.
naming.note: Lexical rules for path segments. Declared here so the resolver and the artifact_workdir helper cannot drift apart on what a legal segment is.

state_root.note: Ability/Skill state namespaces live UNDER state/serveros/<namespace>, never at state/<namespace>. The srv-0003 C1 correction.

run-output.note: A run WITH an Item. project/ITEM/RUN are all path levels.

note: A Skill run with NO Item: skills/<skill>/<RUN>, two levels.
project is run metadata/scope, NOT a directory level. The previous
template skills/<skill>/<project>/<RUN> was cancelled because it
inserted a project directory the machine's actual runs do not have.
The 17 existing runs already match the corrected layout; nothing is
migrated, because nothing was wrong on disk -- the template was.

_comment: C2: record requirements are driven by the record's SEMANTIC ROLE, not by the
records root. A flat records.requires=[project,item] would wrongly reject
records/managed-documents/. This map is illustrative and open-ended: the
resolution rule is 'look up the role', not 'enumerate every record type'.

forbidden_patterns.note: Substitute roots that shadow DATA_ROOT buckets.

forbidden_patterns.match: workspace/<child> where child not in workspace_root_children
forbidden_patterns.note: NO NEW DEBT. Additions are rejected before creation; existing legacy paths are LEGACY_COMPAT, never retro-DENY.

forbidden_patterns.match: state/<namespace> where namespace not in {serveros, personal}
forbidden_patterns.note: state/ is a DATA_ROOT root whose ServerOS-owned child is state/serveros. state/<ns> is the pre-C1 shape.
